1989-2000.what: repainted, the first coat in decades; the cafe stays in the ground-floor shop
1989-2000.why: the cafe's owners bought the house and painted it (1996)

1989-2000.what: a shopfront across two window bays appears in the ground floor, with a bakery in it
1989-2000.why: the owners let the ground floor as a bakery as trade came back to the quay road (1997)

1989-2000.what: upper-floor windows replaced with copies of the 1879 originals, and the house repainted
1989-2000.why: the upper flat's new owners restored it (1998)

1989-2000.what: no deliberate change; it stays boarded and empty, and the roof begins to leak, so it looks worse
1989-2000.why: the heirs cannot agree to sell (1995)

1989-2000.what: the house is left empty and starts to look neglected
1989-2000.why: the last owner died and the heirs, who live away, left it empty (1993)

2000-2010.what: the cafe leaves and the shop in the ground floor stands empty (shopfront still there)
2000-2010.why: the cafe moved to a bigger room on the square as the quay road's trade went up the hill (2009)

2000-2010.what: a balcony over the lane is added, and the house repainted
2000-2010.why: the owners added the balcony and painted with it (2003)

2000-2010.what: boards taken off every window and door, new windows copied from the old ones, house repainted; no longer empty
2000-2010.why: a young family bought the empty house and restored it with the city's help (2007)

2000-2010.what: all windows and doors boarded up

2010-2020.what: the shopfront is removed and the ground floor becomes a home with windows copied from the 1912 ones; repainted
2010-2020.why: no one rented the shop after the oil-price fall, so the owners made a flat, and the city's rules for the wooden town asked for copies of the old windows (2016)

2010-2020.what: back wall (facing down the lane) gets new factory 'old style' windows; whole house repainted
2010-2020.why: the ground-floor flat's owner changed the back windows (2011); upkeep repaint (2013). The 2011 change falls just before 2010-2020 if you count from 2010, so it is small

2010-2020.what: no change in look; still boarded and empty, a bit more run-down

A.claim: Built in 1912 as a jugend-style house with a mansard roof by a cannery owner; the upper floor and roof have never been altered
In 1931 the cannery owner's widow let the ground floor as a shop and a shopfront was fitted; an ironmonger ran it until he retired in 1974
A cafe opened in the empty shop in 1988 and the owners later bought the house and painted it in 1996, the first coat since 1949
The cafe moved off the quay road in 2009 because trade had gone up the hill; the shop stood empty for years
In 2016 the shopfront was removed and the ground floor became a flat, with windows copied from the 1912 originals as the city's wooden-town rules asked

B.claim: A chalet-style boat-builder's house from 1884 burned down in a chimney fire in 1935
It was rebuilt in 1936 as a two-storey functionalist house with a flat roof, so the present house is the 1936 one
A bakery shopfront was fitted in 1997 when trade returned to the quay road
A balcony over the lane was added and the house painted in 2003
It is the best-kept house of the five, repainted in 1987, 2003 and 2017

C.claim: Built in 1879 by a cooper as a storey-and-a-half chalet-style house
In 1971 all windows were replaced cheaply, losing the original look
In 1998 the upper flat's new owners put back copies of the 1879 windows upstairs and repainted; the ground floor kept its 1971 windows
In 2011 the ground-floor flat's owner fitted factory 'old style' windows in the back wall facing down the lane, then the house was repainted in 2013
It has been split into upper and ground-floor flats with different owners, which explains the mixed windows

D.claim: Built in 1828 by a fisherman as a storey-and-a-half empire-style house on the rock outcrop
A lean-to shed was added at the back in 1950 and the front windows were replaced in 1965
After the owner died in 1986 the heirs, who live in Oslo, left it empty with all windows and doors boarded up; by 1995 the roof leaked
A young family bought the empty house in 2007, took the boards down, and restored it with the city's help, with window copies taken from the old ones left in the gables, and painted it
Since 2007 it has been lived in and not repainted (13 years by 2020)

E.claim: Built in 1826 by a fisherman as a small storey-and-a-half empire-style house at the top of the lane
After the last owner died in 1993 the heirs living away left it empty and it has not been looked after since
It was boarded up after a break-in in 2008 and was still empty in 2015
It is the longest-neglected house and the one the view up the lane ends on, so the lane's top looks abandoned
